(per Hon'ble Sri Justice R. Raghunandan Rao) I.A.No.1 of 2024 in W.A.No.1001 of 2023 & I.A.No.3 of 2024 in W.A.No.135 of 2024 Heard Sri Sita Ram Chaparla,
learned counsel for the Review Petitioners and Sri B. S. Shivaji, learned Standing Counsel for the respondents.
2. The Review Petitioners, in both these applications, had approached this Court, by way of W.P.No.34565 of 2022, being aggrieved by the acquisition of their lands under the National Highways HC J & RRR, J I.A.No.1 of 2024 in W.A.No.1001 of 2023 & I.A.No.3 of 2024 in W.A.No.135 of 2024 Act, 1965 (here-in-after referred to as "the Act"), for the purpose of extension of the National Highways in West Godavari District.
3.
The case of the petitioners, before the Learned Single Judge, was that, notification under Section 3A of the Act, dated 07.12.2018, was given for acquiring 3.5954 Hectares of land.

In the subsequent proceedings, the authorities, having decided to reduce the width of the National Highway, issued a notification under Section 3D of the Act and later on, under Section 3G of the Act, reducing the extent of land being acquired to 2.1395 Hectares.

The Learned Single Judge, by his Judgment, dated 21.09.2023, had partly allowed the Writ Petition, holding that notification under Section 3G of the Act, reducing the extent of land mentioned in Section 3A of the Act, is not permissible and that a fresh notification would have to be issued under Section 3G of the Act in consonance with the notification under Section 3A of the Act and to determine the compensation payable to the petitioners in accordance with law, i.e., the Learned Single Judge directed that the authorities would have to acquire the entire extent of 3.5954 Hectares of land.
4.
Aggrieved by this order, both the petitioners as well as the National Highway Authorities of India had approached this Court, by way of W.A.No.1001 of 2023 and W.A.No.135 of 2024.
HC J & RRR, J I.A.No.1 of 2024 in W.A.No.1001 of 2023 & I.A.No.3 of 2024 in W.A.No.135 of 2024 5.

The case of the appellants, in W.A.No.1001 of 2023, was that the Learned Single Judge should have declared the entire process of acquisition to be null and void and that a fresh notification be issued under Section 3A of the Act.

sentences.text: The contention of the National Highway Authorities was that a fresh notification under Section 3G of the Act could not have been directed as there was no prohibition in reducing the extent of land notified under Section 3A of the Act, while issuing the notification under Section 3G of the Act.

7. This Court, after hearing both sides, passed an order, dated 22.08.2024, by partly allowing W.A.No.135 of 2024, on the ground that, compensation for the entire extent of land cannot be directed when the authorities were taking only a part of the land.

This Court also dismissed W.A.No.1001 of 2023, declining to accept the contention of the appellants therein, that the acquisition proceedings should be vitiated on account of non-payment of compensation in the year 2018.
This view was taken as the said ground was not raised before the Learned Single Judge.

This Court had also held that the contention of the appellants therein, that fresh notification, under Section 3A of the Act, should have been issued, cannot be accepted as the land is vested with the Central Government by virtue of Section 3D of the Act.
HC J & RRR, J I.A.No.1 of 2024 in W.A.No.1001 of 2023 & I.A.No.3 of 2024 in W.A.No.135 of 2024 8.

The Review Petitioners have now moved the present set of Review Applications, contending that the vesting of land under Section 3D of the Act would not have any relevance on the question of whether the acquisition process had been done properly or not.

The Review Petitioners contend that, once there is a defect in the acquisition process, the land-losers can be compensated, even if the land is already vested with the State, by postponing the date on which the market value is to be taken into account for the purpose of calculating the compensation.

The Review Petitioners contend that, in similar circumstances, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in the case of Competent Authority vs. Barangore Jute Factory & Ors.1, had held that while the acquisition process was flawed, the same need not be set aside and the land-losers can be adequately compensated by postponing the date for calculation, as on which the market value is to be fixed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
9. The Review Petitioners, on the basis of the above grounds, contend that this Court having held that the land has vested with the State, by virtue of the notification under Section 3D of the Act,
should have followed the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Barangore Jute Factory Case (supra) and the non-application of these principles is an error apparent on the face of the record.

(2005) 13 SCC 477 HC J & RRR, J I.A.No.1 of 2024 in W.A.No.1001 of 2023 &
I.A.No.3 of 2024 in W.A.No.135 of 2024 10.

entities.text: (2005) 13 SCC 477 HC J & RRR, J I.A.No.1 of 2024
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The question of complying with the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Barangore Jute Factory Case (supra), would arise when a finding is given that the acquisition process itself should be set aside, but larger public interest would be affected, if such an order is passed.
In the present case, this Court has not given any finding that the acquisition process itself is flawed or that, it is to be set aside.
In such circumstances, the application of Barangore Jute Factory Case (supra) would not arise.
11. Consequently, there is no error on the face of the record which requires this Court to review the earlier orders.
